title: Rational and $\Qlb$ purity
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated morphism of pure relative dimension $d$
between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $K$ lie in the $E$-coefficient
category of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], respectively the
$\Qlb$-coefficient category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], presented
by a normalized integral system (a lattice) as in
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Then

$$
\gamma_{f,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$

is an isomorphism in the corresponding category: rationalization along
[prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] and finite extension of coefficient
fields carry the adic purity isomorphism of
[thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] to the $E$- and $\Qlb$-purity
isomorphisms.

proof.text: Step 1a (geometric domain). The field $k$ is noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure morphisms of $X$ and $Y$, and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] over $k$. Thus both schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional. Since $\ell\ne p$, $\ell$ is invertible on them. They therefore satisfy the scheme hypotheses in [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Choose an integral lattice $K_0$ presenting the given rational object and write $Q_E$ for rationalization.

Step 1b (uniform Tor domain). By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], the integral category underlying the rationalization is exactly [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] on these schemes. In particular $K_0$ is derived complete and its first reduction is bounded; choose an interval $[r,s]$ containing its cohomology. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], every reduction has Tor amplitude in that same interval. Consequently $K_0\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, including when $K_0$ is a torsion lattice.

source.place: Step 1, the lattice belongs to the adic finite-Tor category

proof.text: Step 1c (compatible integral choice). Set $H_E=Lf_E^*(-)(d)[2d]$ and $G_E=Rf_E^!$. The preceding domain checks and the stated smooth separated pure-dimensional hypotheses allow [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] to be applied to every lattice. It supplies an integral isomorphism with the prescribed finite reductions, without uniqueness of coherent lifts. Choose the simultaneous family $\gamma_{E,K_0}:H_EK_0\to G_EK_0$ supplied by [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. Its statement supplies the exact linear functors, integral linear naturality and coefficient compatibility, with exactly those reductions. All subsequent maps use this compatible choice.

source.place: Step 1, adic purity for the lattice with a compatible choice

proof.text: Step 1d (localization). Apply [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to the exact integral linear functors $H_E,G_E$ and their chosen natural transformation. It extends the transformation to all localized morphisms, with component $Q_E(\gamma_{E,K_0})$. The rational pullback and tensor formulas of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the rational twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] identify its source with $Lf_E^*(Q_EK_0)(d)[2d]$; [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] defines its target as $Rf_E^!(Q_EK_0)$. The inverse is $Q_E(\gamma_{E,K_0}^{-1})$: the two inverse identities follow by functoriality. Naturality, supplied for all rational morphisms by the cited transport theorem, applies in particular to rational isomorphisms between lattice presentations, so these components are independent of presentation.

source.place: Step 1, rational transport and lattice independence

proof.text:
Step 2 (finite extensions and their equations). For $E\subset F$, let $T_{F/E}$ be [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The helper's integral $C_{F/E,W}$ is ordinary tensor by the completed coefficient sheaf, as is the integral functor underlying this $T$. The natural isomorphism $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies it with the strict inverse-limit scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]; its hypothesis holds because the lattices are derived complete. Thus there is no identification of these two constructions by definition alone. Work in the helper's ordinary-tensor presentation, whose associator is precisely the tensor associator specified in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. For the simultaneously chosen integral family of Step 1, rationalize the natural comparison equation of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. Since $T_{F/E}=Q_FC_{F/E}$ on integral representatives, this gives, on every object,
$$b_{F/E,K}\,T_{F/E,X}(\gamma_{E,K})=\gamma_{F,T_{F/E,Y}K}\,a_{F/E,K}.$$
For the coefficient-passage exceptional functor defined in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], use the rationalized integral $b$ as its scalar comparison. The helper identifies that integral map with the adjunction mate and proves its coherence, so no independent Verdier-duality comparison is needed. The twist comparison is the coefficient comparison of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The identity and composition equations in the integral helper remain equations after applying rationalization; the helper also gives shift compatibility of both exact comparisons. Hence the displayed equation respects the unit, shifts and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Solving it for inverses gives
$$T_{F/E,X}(\gamma_{E,K}^{-1})\,b_{F/E,K}^{-1}=a_{F/E,K}^{-1}\,\gamma_{F,T_{F/E,Y}K}^{-1}.$$
Thus both the purity family and its inverse satisfy the finite-stage compatibility required for descent.

source.place: Proof, Step 2 (Qbar-stage): compatibility of finite coefficient extensions, made explicit before common-stage descent

proof.text: Step 3a (common-stage descent). In [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], objects are pairs $(E,K)$ and morphisms are common-stage classes $[M,u]$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] to the rational exact families $H_E,G_E$, using the comparisons $a,b$ of Step 2. That step verifies precisely the unit, associator and shift hypotheses for both families, and the compatibility square for $\gamma$. The theorem explicitly descends compatible natural transformations and their equations, not just functors. It therefore descends this family to a natural transformation $\overline\gamma:H\Rightarrow G$, with component represented by $\gamma_{E,K}$. Its representative formula gives the functor actions $a_F^{-1}H_M(u)a_E$ and $b_F^{-1}G_M(u)b_E$; independence of enlargement and of the class representative is part of the cited descent assertion.

source.place: Step 2, common-stage representatives and natural-transformation descent

proof.text: Step 3b (inverse and conclusion). The inverse family satisfies the coefficient square established in Step 2, so [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] descends it too, along with the equations $\gamma_{E,K}^{-1}\gamma_{E,K}=1$ and $\gamma_{E,K}\gamma_{E,K}^{-1}=1$. Hence $\overline\gamma$ is an isomorphism. The common-stage pullback, tensor and twist definitions in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the coefficient-passage exceptional functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], identify $H(K)=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$ and $G(K)=Rf^!K$. These are the claimed $\Qlb$ purity maps, transported from the rational maps and independent of the finite stage.

source.place: Step 2, inverse equations and identification with Qbar operations

proof_origin.place: Steps 1 and 2, preserving the returned localization / finite extension / common-stage route; existing generic transport nodes replace inline arguments

blueprint_update.statement:
Work in the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], let
$f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of relative dimension $d$ over a
separated finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $K$ lie in the $E$-coefficient
category of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], respectively the
$\Qlb$-coefficient category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], presented
by a normalized integral system (a lattice) as in
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Then

$$
\gamma_{f,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$

is an isomorphism in the corresponding category: rationalization along
[prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] and finite extension of coefficient
fields carry the adic purity isomorphism of
[thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] to the $E$- and $\Qlb$-purity
isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Step 1: the $E$-stage. An $E$-object $K$ of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category] is presented by a lattice
$K_{\mathcal O_E}\in D^b_{ctf}(\cdot,\mathcal O_E)$ with
$K_E=K_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}E$. The adic purity
isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{f,K_{\mathcal O_E}}:\ Lf^*K_{\mathcal O_E}(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K_{\mathcal O_E}
$$

of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] for the lattice, extended along
the exact functor $-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}E$ (exact because
$\mathcal O_E\to E$ is flat), is an isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{f,K_E}:\ Lf^*K_E(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K_E
$$

between the $E$-objects, i.e. the $E$-purity isomorphism of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Step 2: the $\Qlb$-stage.
A $\Qlb$-object of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is represented
by an $E$-object $K_E$ for some finite $E/\Ql$ (no idempotent is
needed, the finite-stage categories being idempotent complete); the
$\Qlb$-purity isomorphism is the transport of the $E$-purity
isomorphism of Step 1 along the scalar extension
$E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$, well defined by the independence of
[prop-pur-rational-purity-transitivity-summands].
